label: Late encoding positions (t >= 6) and the <DEL> step
explanation: Fires only near the end of the encoding phase: on original-token steps at t >= 6 and on the <DEL> step (recall_idx 0). It never fires at t <= 2 or anywhere in the copy phase after <DEL>. The firing rate climbs with position: orig_idx 5: 5%, 6: 21%, 7: 46%, 8: 68%; at <DEL> it is 24%. So it is mostly a long-sequence (L 8-9) unit. The strongest activations come at the last original tokens and at <DEL> in 9-token sequences. Which tokens appeared earlier in the sequence affects whether it fires: sequences starting with or containing p/o/r/a/m/i/k/d fire more often, and sequences built mostly from letters like e/w/n/l often stay silent even at late positions. Requiring at least 3 such earlier tokens raises dev F1 only from 0.53 to 0.61, so the predicate leaves that out. The predicate covers about 96% of activation mass but has low precision (about 0.37), because many late-position steps stay below threshold.
